Speaking of prey, I'll focus mainly on its DLC called mooncrash, the basic idea is that you play as a simulation operator (he's a nigger by the way, but strangely enough, his wife and kid are both negros, it's not an interracial relationship) so anyway, he uses a highly advanced simulator that allows him to relive memories of workers on a moon base that was infested with alien organism to find out what happened to them, did they escape or not and if yes then how, you can relive the memories of 5 characters (remember the characters I talked about above? The black woman engineer and the Indian security guy.. Etc? Yeas those are the ones) you start with only one of them then gradually unlock the other 4.

While you're supposed to see memories that already happened, in reality you control those characters so you write the memory yourself

There are a lot of fun things about this dlc (if you could look past the wokeness) every time you replay, a lot of elements change, weapons and item placements, enemy types and positions

There are even environmental changes that differ with each run, sometimes you may find one of the rooms contaminated with nuclear waste, sometimes you may find doors to some rooms destroyed, making said rooms inaccessible, some of your characters have special skills like repairing broken doors or shape shifting into small objects allowing them to squeeze through, sometimes you need to look around may find an air ventilation or maintenance access that might be connected to the rooms you want to get into, sometimes there is no way to get into that room and you'll have to leave it to another run

Sometimes you may find rooms on fire and must use special glue to put it out, sometimes you may find an entire section out of power and in darkness which can help you stealth past monsters but on the downside many electric door won't open so you'll have to get creative and find alternative routes to navigate through the area or look for the power control room and restore electricity to that sector, sometimes you may find sectors flooded with water, and sometimes you may find junction boxes busted and emitting electrical surges, if these two randomly generated environmental elements were present in the same sector, it'll be hard to get around as you'll be forced to jump on top of objects that are not dipped deeply in the water in order not to get electrocuted

You can find many blue prints for weapons, ammunition and items, once found, you may create desired item in fabricator stations scattered around the moon base, or can buy the items when you change character (you can only select a different character when the one you currently play with has either managed to escape the moon base or got killed) every action you do like killing enemies, escaping successfully, finishing side quests that are randomly generated or finding key items will reward you with sim points which you can use to buy items before you start your next adventure

There are also neuromods that are basically skill points, each character has access to different skills, and each skill you unlock remains permanently unlike items that are lost with every new run and must be bought again with sim points before you begin

There are human skills and alien skills, if you unlocked too many alien skills for certain characters, those characters might be treated by security systems as aliens, some gates that automatically close when an alien is nearby will close in the face of those characters too, and anti-alien turrets will shoot you on sight.

one great tool is the disruptor gun that shoots electrical current which temporarily disables mechanical systems as well as mechanical enemies, actually there is a neat trick you can use with that gun, even if your character itself wasn't treated by security systems as an alien, sometimes the anti alien gates will still activate their barriers if there are other aliens close by, preventing you from getting through and telling you to eliminate every nearby alien first before the gates shut down the barrier, you might be in no condition to fight all of the aliens nearby, you could be on the brink of death or don't have enough ammo to kill them all... Etc, so you can use your disruptor gun and shoot the computer near the gate, this will temporarily disable the barrier, be careful though, if an alien was chasing you, it might get past the gate too while it's disabled

Despite the game's setting that is similar to dead space, still prey doesn't feel that scary, a bit creepy but the game is not that dark and there is no ambient sounds that'll have looking over your shoulder, you won't hear the sounds the monsters make unless you're too close and is engaging them, many monster sounds are more annoying than scary, the scariest monster is the poltergeist, not only is it invisible, but the sound it makes is also creepy, not to mention that sometimes it uses telekinesis to manipulate objects around you and even throw them at you when you least expect it

There is still much more to be said about prey in general and it's moon crash DLC in particular, especially with its too many randomly generated elements as well as the corruption system which I didn't mention in my review and how dead characters may sometimes be infected and turned into alien monsters, but I'll leave it up to you to discover, if you're interested in prey and dishonored despite the extremely heavy amounts of pozz, off course I wouldn't recommend paying more than 10$ for both of them due to their wokeness, and it'll be even better if you could get them for free
